EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours have witnessed a significant military escalation between the United States and Iran, marked by widespread US airstrikes on various military and infrastructure targets across southern Iran, and Iran's retaliatory missile and drone attacks against US military assets in Gulf states and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Compounding this, the US has announced the immediate resumption of its naval blockade targeting Iranian ports, further intensifying economic pressure and regional tensions.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran include a five-hour wave of US strikes on July 13, as announced by CENTCOM, targeting military objectives in Bushehr, Chabahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, and Bandar Abbas. These precision strikes aimed to degrade Iran's ability to attack commercial shipping. Iranian media also reported US attacks in Mahshahr and Abadan. In response, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed to have launched new drone attacks against US forces, defense systems, and missile sites in Kuwait. Iran's Navy claimed to have shot down an American drone in Bandar Abbas. Separately, Iran reported using unmanned surface vessels against a ship repair facility in Bandar Abbas. Casualties and infrastructure damage include US projectiles striking near water and power stations on Kish Island, damaging technical parameters and several vessels in the harbor, which may lead to power outages. An alleged US airstrike in northern Hormozgan Province reportedly killed family members of an Iranian park ranger. Initial assessments in Bushehr Province's Dashti and Tangestan areas reported no fatalities. Iran stated a railway bridge attacked last week by the US was repaired within 24 hours. Air defense performance included the downing of an American drone in Bandar Abbas and two other drones over southern Iran. The internal political situation saw former President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad attend an economic committee meeting, refuting claims of his house arrest or ties to Israel. Parliament introduced a bill titled "Strategic Action for the Security and Sustainable Progress of the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf" to assert control over the waterway. Iran executed two members of the Daesh terrorist group for armed rebellion. Economically, Iran's petroleum minister, Mohsen Paknejad, affirmed continued oil exports despite revoked US sanctions waivers, noting large reserves were cleared during the previous blockade lift. Iran’s leadership, including Brigadier General Akrami-Nia, warned the US against aggression in Hormuz, asserting that respect for Iranian rights is the only way to reopen the strait. A new mural in Tehran's Palestine Square explicitly threatened the families of Trump and Netanyahu. Iran submitted a formal complaint to the UN Security Council regarding US violations of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included IDF strikes in Gaza that killed Osama Naim Hamdi Shamlakh, a Hamas naval force commander, and three other armed Hamas gunmen. Seven Palestinians were reportedly killed in a drone strike on a police station in northern Gaza, and another four were killed in Jabalia. Israeli artillery strikes were reported in Qunine and Al-Hajir valley in Southern Lebanon, with drone strikes in Nabatieh al-Fouqa. Regarding home front air defense, a reported explosion in central Israel is under IDF investigation. Fires were reported near Margaliot and Netivot. Politically, the Knesset approved a controversial law to freeze arrests of Haredi deserters (also referred to as "Fundamental Law: Torah Study") with vote counts varying between 58-54 and 63-52. Prime Minister Netanyahu was initially absent but later arrived to vote in favor. Coalition members Sharan Haskel (who resigned as Deputy Foreign Minister), Yuli Edelstein, Moshe Solomon, and Dan Illouz voted against the bill. Opposition leaders, including Lapid, Gantz, Bennett, and Liberman, condemned the law and filed petitions to the High Court of Justice. Defense Minister Israel Katz formally requested a pardon for former soldier Elor Azaria, which the IDF Chief of Staff, Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, opposed due to Azaria's lack of remorse. The Cabinet approved 1.3 billion NIS ($347 million) for 34 new settlements in the West Bank and a $2.3 billion framework agreement for 12,000 new housing units. Civilian impact includes public condemnation of the conscription law, an alleged kidnapping in Yavne (criminal, 5 arrested), police thwarting a criminal attack in Umm al-Fahm, and arson incidents at a Jerusalem light rail site and Japnica restaurants. Netanyahu, visiting Dimona, warned Iran that any future attack on Israel would be met with a "much more powerful" and different response.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, the IDF announced the elimination of Osama Naim Hamdi Shamlakh, a Hamas naval force commander, and three armed Hamas gunmen in separate strikes. Press TV reported seven Palestinians killed in a drone strike on a north Gaza police station, and four killed in Jabalia. No specific updates on the humanitarian situation were provided. There were no direct reports on ceasefire or negotiation status. Settler activity was noted with a group of Israeli settler activists from the Uri Tzafon Movement illegally crossing into Lebanon and another group, the Bashan Pioneers, attempting to cross into Syria, both incidents condemned by the IDF. Additionally, dozens of Eliezer Berland's followers entered the Palestinian village of Kifl Haris in the West Bank to protest access limitations to Jewish holy sites, with two reportedly injured but refusing evacuation due to fear of arrest. The Israeli Cabinet approved 1.3 billion NIS for 34 new settlements in the West Bank, and Israel signed a $2.3 billion agreement to expand illegal West Bank settlements by 12,000 units.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations were referenced with an image shared by Press TV showing an "Israeli military vehicle destroyed by Hezbollah resistance movement." Israeli strikes included reports of artillery fire in Qunine and Al-Hajir valley in Southern Lebanon, and drone strikes in Nabatieh al-Fouqa. There were no reports of UNIFIL incidents or large-scale displacement. Cross-border exchanges included a fire near Margaliot, close to the Israeli-Lebanese border, and Israeli settler activists illegally crossing into Lebanon before being returned by the IDF.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, Israeli settler activists attempted to illegally cross the border from the southern Golan Heights into Syrian territory and were detained by the IDF. In Iraq, Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi met with US President Trump, stating his intention to confine weapons to state control. The Nujaba movement, an Iraqi resistance group, warned of FPV drone operations against US bases in Iraq. Iranian missiles were reportedly launched against a camp of Iranian-Kurdish opposition forces in northern Iraq. A limited fire broke out at Basra International Airport. Iraqi PM Ali Al-Zaidi is scheduled to visit Tehran next week. Trump expressed affection for Iraq and suggested that US troops might not be needed for protection, while major US oil companies were expected to enter the country.

GULF STATES
Kuwait experienced missile and drone attacks targeting US military assets, with sirens sounding and strong explosions reported. The Kuwaiti army confirmed responding to "hostile aerial targets" in its airspace, with some reports indicating Iranian projectiles hitting Kuwaiti territory near the Iraqi border. Bahrain reported explosions and emergency sirens, with Iranian media claiming US targets were attacked there. The UAE confirmed two of its oil tankers, "Mombasa" and "Al-Bahiyah," were struck by Iranian anti-ship missiles off Oman's coast, resulting in one crew fatality and eight injuries. The UAE Foreign Ministry condemned these attacks as piracy and demanded the unconditional reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The US Embassy in Abu Dhabi and Consulate in Dubai canceled consular appointments and remain on "mandatory evacuation." Saudi Arabia was targeted by six ballistic missiles and drones from Houthi forces at Abha International Airport; Houthis warned all airlines to avoid Saudi airspace until the blockade on Sanaa International Airport is lifted. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) received Trump's approval for military action against Houthis in Yemen. Oman's Foreign Ministry affirmed its commitment to restoring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz through transparent and impartial cooperation. The European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) issued a warning for airlines to avoid airspace over Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and parts of the Gulf of Oman through July 29 due to heightened risks.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Widespread US Strikes in Iran:** CENTCOM announced the completion of a five-hour wave of strikes on July 13 against Iranian military targets in Bushehr, Chabahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, and Bandar Abbas, marking the third consecutive night of US operations.
2.  **Iranian Retaliation and Shipping Attacks:** Iran launched missile and drone attacks reportedly targeting US military assets in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan (King Faisal Air Base, Muwaffaq Salti airbase). Iranian missiles also struck two Emirati oil tankers, "Mombasa" and "Al-Bahiyah," off Oman's coast, resulting in one fatality and eight injuries.
3.  **US Naval Blockade Reinstated:** The US announced the resumption of its naval blockade on Iranian ports, effective July 14, 23:30 UTC, targeting vessels entering or departing Iranian ports and coastal areas.
4.  **Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia:** Houthi forces claimed responsibility for six ballistic missile and drone attacks on Abha International Airport in Saudi Arabia and issued warnings to all airlines to avoid Saudi airspace.
5.  **Israeli Settlement Expansion Approved:** The Israeli Cabinet approved 1.3 billion NIS ($347 million) for the establishment and development of 34 new settlements in the West Bank, supported by a $2.3 billion framework agreement for 12,000 new housing units.
6.  **Controversial Israeli Conscription Law Passed:** The Knesset passed a law to freeze arrests of Haredi deserters (vote count discrepancies between 58-54 and 63-52), prompting strong political backlash and High Court petitions.
7.  **EASA Issues Gulf Airspace Warning:** The European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) warned airlines to avoid airspace over Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and parts of the Gulf of Oman until July 29 due to risks of "misidentification" and "unintended engagement."
8.  **Trump's Shifting Hormuz Policy:** President Trump reversed his proposed 20% transit toll for the Strait of Hormuz, announcing instead that Gulf states would make large investments in the US. He reiterated that the Strait is open for all but Iranian vessels and that Iran will not possess nuclear weapons.
9.  **Netanyahu's Warning to Iran:** Israeli PM Netanyahu, speaking from Dimona, issued a strong warning to Iran, stating that any attack on Israel would be met with a "much more powerful" and different response.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The direct military confrontation between the US and Iran carries an extremely high risk of further escalation. Active flashpoints include southern Iran (Bushehr, Chabahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, Bandar Abbas, Mahshahr, Abadan), US military bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan, and the Strait of Hormuz, where the US blockade and Iranian naval actions are ongoing. Trump's rhetoric regarding hitting Iran "very hard" and potentially striking "Pickaxe Mountain" (Karkas), a suspected nuclear site, indicates a willingness to target highly sensitive locations, which Iran has warned would turn the region into "hell." The US maintains over 50,000 military personnel in the Middle East and is increasing its strike tempo. Saudi Arabia, backed by Trump, is preparing for intensified military action against Houthis, suggesting a widening of the Yemen conflict. Red lines include Trump's firm stance against Iran possessing nuclear weapons and Iran's warning of devastating retaliation if its core strategic sites are attacked.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture, as articulated by President Trump, includes renewed military operations against Iran, described as "limited, measured, and planned" defensive actions. Trump announced the resumption of the naval blockade on Iranian ports effective July 15 and rescinded his proposed 20% Hormuz toll in favor of investment deals from Gulf states. He reiterated that a deal with Iran is possible but accused Iran of not honoring agreements. Trump also approved Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's request for military action against the Houthis. US consular services in the UAE have been curtailed. Gulf states, including Kuwait, Bahrain, UAE, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia, are directly affected by or reacting to the conflict. Kuwait reported attacks on US military assets. The UAE condemned attacks on commercial shipping as piracy and demanded the Strait's unconditional reopening. Saudi Arabia faces Houthi attacks and has US backing for a Yemen campaign. Oman maintains a neutral stance, upholding freedom of navigation. European Union members have seen EASA warn against flights over Gulf airspace. The EU's debate on trade restrictions with Israeli settlements remains contentious. The Czech Republic is pursuing air defense systems from Israel. Russia's Foreign Minister Lavrov condemned US strikes as violating the Islamabad MoU, potentially closing avenues for resolution. China called for de-escalation and safe passage in Hormuz but showed signs of growing unease with Russia's dependency and alignment with North Korea. Turkey issued an arrest warrant for Israeli PM Netanyahu for alleged "crimes against humanity" and "genocide." Pakistan is reportedly engaged in mediation efforts between the US and Iran.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several discrepancies and unverified claims are present in the intelligence feed. The exact vote count for the Israeli conscription law varies between 58-54 and 63-52, and its precise legal title is inconsistently reported (Law to freeze arrests of Haredi deserters vs. Fundamental Law: Torah Study). Trump's shifting stance on a 20% Hormuz transit toll, first reported as "very serious" then replaced with investment deals, indicates either rapid policy changes or conflicting internal communications. Reports of former Iranian President Ahmadinejad's alleged house arrest and ties to Israel are contradicted by Iranian media showing his public appearance, suggesting a counter-narrative or disinformation. US Senator Roger Marshall's claim of "hundreds of soldiers" lost by the US significantly exceeds official reporting and is unverified. Iranian media reports of US strikes in Mahshahr and Abadan are not explicitly listed in CENTCOM's broader target list, although Mahshahr is in Khuzestan Province, a reported target area. The nature of naval encounters also varies: CENTCOM reported using suicide USVs against a ship repair facility in Bandar Abbas, while Iran reported shooting down an American drone in the same area. Specifics of damage and casualties from Iranian attacks on US bases in Gulf states (Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan) are largely based on IRGC claims or local unverified reports, lacking explicit US confirmation of specific hits or casualty figures. Propaganda indicators include the new mural in Tehran and the highly charged rhetoric from both US and Iranian leaders, often aimed at domestic audiences. There are reporting gaps regarding the full economic impact of the renewed US naval blockade and detailed assessments of the Islamabad MoU's provisions and alleged violations.
